hyps.why: Raising an already large learning rate destabilises training and caused large drops in rows 47-48 and 49 (vehicle).
At very small learning rates the 243-epoch run is undertrained, so a larger rate helps on all three datasets (rows 41-43).
Stepping down from a divergent-range learning rate recovers accuracy, with large gains in rows 51-54.
Strong L2 penalty (about 0.13 to 1) underfits, so reducing it improves accuracy, most strongly in rows 11, 12 and 19.
Increasing an already strong L2 penalty worsens underfitting, as in rows 9 and 10.
Very small batches give noisy updates, so a larger batch tends to help (rows 21-24 and 26).
At large batch sizes, going smaller mostly hurt (rows 31 and 32), although row 33 was an exception.
Deeper networks at high learning rates become unstable, with big losses in rows 62, 66 and 68.
Removing a layer stabilises training at high learning rates, as in rows 72, 77 and 79.
Wider networks combined with large learning rates are more prone to divergence, as in rows 88 and 90.
